takeaways: SAP S/4HANA is an ERP system rebuilt on the in-memory, column-based HANA database, which lets analytics and transactions run on one shared copy of the data.
Every company on SAP ECC must choose a deployment model and a migration path (greenfield, brownfield or bluefield) before mainstream maintenance ends in 2027.
Keeping a clean core and integrating through Microsoft Fabric, Entra ID and Power Platform connectors pays off in upgrades, while data cleanup and process change are the real cost of migration.
hook: SAP S/4HANA sounds intimidating, yet most companies running SAP ECC have to decide where it lives and how to migrate before the 2027 deadline. This plain-language episode is for IT and business people who need to understand what S/4HANA is, how it connects to Microsoft tools, and where projects usually go wrong.
